Cresting the soapsud ridge, the cadmium yellow hollow rubber duck lifts completely clear, water sheeting off its breast, the wake still fanning wide behind it across the whole surface.

Going down bow-first into the drain whirlpool, a cobalt blue hollow plastic boat tilts past vertical, its flanks and panels one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted anchor.
Breaking through the steam fog already close, the scarlet hollow rubber duck's beak emerges first, mould seam glistening, the rest of the fleet surfacing rank by rank behind it.
Heeling violently away on both sides as a dented hollow plastic fin in ox-blood red cuts between two hulls, foam curling off its leading edge, both vessels leaning hard over.
Hauling the plug chain taut with the brass key still turning on its flank, the wind-up hollow plastic frog strains forward, chain dripping as it lifts, wake fanning wide astern.
Running before a breaking crest with the whole line stern-on, every scuffed rubber hull surfing the same swell, the last one still climbing while the leaders have already begun their descent.

Coming alongside the capsized chrome-yellow hollow rubber duck, the squat orange hollow plastic tugboat has its ribbon line already across, its flanks and panels one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted stripe.

Surfacing directly under the leader, the grey hollow plastic submarine lifts the cadmium yellow duck bodily upward, water parting around both, the submarine's flanks one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted chevron.
Spinning slowly in the eddy, a faded lime-green hollow rubber duck faces entirely the wrong way, its mould seam catching the light, while the rest of the fleet goes on past without it.
Turning back hard through its own wake, the large cadmium yellow hollow rubber duck heels into the turn, a lone pale duckling still far astern, the gap between them visibly closing.
Making landfall, the leader's orange beak just touching the grounded bar of soap, water still running off its back from the crossing, the whole fleet pressing in close behind it.

Passing the tap in line abreast, every hull dwarfed by the chrome column rising out of frame above them, water beaded on their scuffed rubber backs, the tap's reflection stretched across the surface below.

Swamped to the gunwales and still going, the hollow plastic red-hulled raft rides so low the water brims at its edges, its flanks and panels one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted star.
Taking the hollow rubber duck down by one foot, the faded violet rubber octopus pulls it under, only the cadmium yellow tail still showing above the surface, the ring still spreading outward.
Rolling right over with its worn pale keel coming up, a sky-blue hollow rubber hull shows its squeaker hole to the sky, the water still closing over its cabin top ahead of it.
Rafted together on the swell, two hollow rubber hulls — one cadmium yellow, one tangerine — are bound with a twist of red ribbon while the water runs in long rolls beneath them both.

Paddling hard against the current and losing ground, the wind-up hollow plastic frog in jade green churns its hind legs at full stroke, its brass key still turning, wake spreading wider than its own length.
Leaning the whole fleet together as the water tilts, every hollow rubber and plastic hull canting the same way, their painted keels lifted on one side, wakes converging toward the low edge.

Collapsing heavy with water, the sodden grey washcloth sail folds and drives the hollow plastic raft broadside into the swell, its flanks and panels one plain block of scuffed painted colour wearing a single small painted spot.
Rolling up under the fleet, the chalk-white hollow plastic whale sends water arcing high over the line of hulls, each duck rising and tipping in sequence down the length of the formation.
Stopped dead in the mirror calm, the entire fleet sits motionless on a surface so still that every cadmium yellow hull and every scuffed red fin has a perfect twin hanging beneath it.
Going over the side of the beaker, the tiny moulded plastic diver in faded orange pitches headfirst into the water, one arm forward, bubbles still rising where it pierced the surface a moment before.

Two scuffed hollow rubber ducks in sun-faded yellow hold position at the rim of the drain whirlpool, watching the cobalt blue hollow plastic vessel spiral below them, the current still pulling their own bows inward.

Breaking out of the steam, bows first, the scarlet hollow rubber duck comes through already at speed, the mist still trailing off its bite-dented beak, the fleet ranked close behind it in a staggered echelon.

Hauling through the gap where the missing vessel was, the remaining hollow rubber hulls close the line without breaking pace, the space already narrowing, only the spreading ring on the water showing where it went down.
